abstract: Cory Doctorow's book-length argument that AI is mostly deployed not to replace workers but to make them serve machines — the 'reverse centaur' configuration. In automation theory a centaur is a human using technology as a tool; a reverse centaur is a human conscripted as a helper to a machine, working at inhuman pace (Amazon delivery drivers tracked second-by-second, warehouse pickers denied bathroom breaks, programmers held to AI-throughput quotas). Doctorow argues the $16T+ AI valuation thesis only mathematically works if AI replaces large swathes of wage labor, and that AI deployers are actively trying to build a class alliance between investors and AI-product-enjoyers against workers. Published 2026 by Farrar, Straus and Giroux; companion talk delivered at University of Washington 'Neuroscience, AI and Society' lecture series.
keyFindings: Reframes AI labor harm as 'reverse centaur' configurations: human serves machine, not vice versa
$16T+ AI valuation thesis is incoherent unless AI substitutes for the human wage bill at scale — the math forces the labor-displacement story
AI deployers attempt to construct a political coalition with AI-product enjoyers against workers; Doctorow argues the better coalition is workers against deployers
Names specific case studies: gig delivery drivers (algorithmic dispatch), warehouse workers (AI-pace quotas), programmers (code-throughput surveillance)
Counters techno-optimist framings by separating capability (often real) from deployment (often coercive)
methodology: Polemical essay / book; synthesizes labor reporting, automation history, and economic critique. Not empirical estimation.
qualifiers: Tier 4 — popular book, advocacy stance. Strong on cases, light on quantitative claims. Best cited as a position-defining text for the reverse-centaur framing, not as evidence on displacement magnitudes.
